newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS Q3 trading results weak, provisions up.
newsitem.headline: UBS Q3 trading results weak, provisions up.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said third quarter results showed declines in its trading income, while provisions also remained higher for the first nine months.
Trading results in the third quarter were weaker than in the second, with declines most evident in foreign exchange and banknote trading, it said in its third-quarter statement.
The statement provided no absolute figures and no percentage comparisons.

Although its trading income on a cumulative basis for the first nine-months remained above that of the previous year, the third quarter alone showed a weaker result, despite improvements in some areas. Equities and fixed-income divisions were positive, but foreign exchange trading results were weak.

"The strongest contribution came from the equities sector. Trading in bonds and in interest rate instruments also continued its positive trend. Income from foreign exchange and banknote trading, however, was down versus a year earlier," UBS said.
"Lower trading volumes in the third quarter had a negative impact on fee and commission income," UBS said.
Brokerage commissions in particular were lower, it said.
But underwriting and corporate finance business continued to turn in a strong performance. "At end-September earnings already exceeded last year's full figure," it said of these results.

"Cumulated for the first nine months of this year, fees and commissions from securities and investment business together made a very pleasing contribution to income," it said, adding that the contribution was "also well up on the year-earlier level."
It also said that a further recovery was noticeable in net interest income, which it said posted a slight year-on-year increase on a cumulative basis.

"Depreciation and write-offs on fixed assets developed as planned," UBS said. It said these were slightly higher than a year ago, mainly due to depreciation which is required to be charged on newly-occupied banking premises.
But, it added that no improvement was seen in value adjustments, provisions and losses, which over three quarters registered "a significant increase versus a year earlier."
"Credit risk provisions continue to relate almost exclusively to the Swiss loan portfolio," it said.
With respect to expenses, it said these developed "in line with expectations." Personnel expenses were higher year-on-year due to accruals for performance-related bonuses, it said.
General administrative expense was slightly higher than a year earlier, "but is under control," UBS said.

Taxes did not register as sharp a jump as in the first half, but "they are still well above the 1995-level. This increase is due to stronger earnings and to the absence this year of the special factors which reduced tax expense substantially in 1995," it said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
